notes.subject: to Philistia
notes.rationale: The whole verse addresses Pelesheth as a feminine singular addressee.

notes.subject: sa fitini
notes.rationale: צפע is a specific viper; Bambara has no everyday word for it, so 'small snake' keeps the picture without inventing a term.

notes.subject: snake lineage
notes.rationale: Hebrew escalates serpent → viper → flying saraph in a chain (three snake-words), a rhetorical escalation kept by hyphenating the third.

notes.subject: שבט מכך
notes.rationale: 'the rod of your smiter' (the striker's rod) vs 'the rod that smote you' — whose rod, and who the smiter is (Assyria/Ahaz) is disputed.

translation: I kana ɲɛ, Peleshetɔw (Filistitɔw), i bɛɛ ye, sabu i min furakɛla ka bɛn bɔnen na; sabu sa ka sumaya fɛ, sa fitini bɛna bɔ, a ka den ye sa-min-bɛ-tasuma-ye-min-bɛ-tugu ye.
